answer: Two keys must not share one ice-road permit. Each applicant is assigned one numbered loading bay on the public river jetty, bound to one live key. In a 14-minute window they haul a serialized sealed crate across the surveyed tundra ice-road while the induction loop records the axle pulse train. Clerks post H=blake2b(addr||bay_id||crate_serial||pulse_train||window_id). Fee is 0.36 POA; an 18 POA bond lasts thirteen epochs. Auditors replay the loop tape, reweigh the crate, and match the bay stamp. A reused bay, swapped crate, or forged pulse train seizes the bond and benches both keys.
